set.prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule: the 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines (https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/2024-2028-plha-formula-guidelines.pdf) contain no prevailing wage provision, and the County's PLHA amendment staff report and Resolution 26-317 certifications (https://legistar.granicus.com/nevco/attachments/7d500d37-79a8-450c-820d-b92b30542adf.pdf) are silent. Coverage of a County PLHA loan is a general Labor Code 1720(b) question that turns on 1720(c) exemptions, including the 1720(c)(6)(E) affordable housing exemption applied in DIR PW 2006-020, and on any HOME or CDBG layered in the trust fund loan.
set.audit_note: Prevailing wage left unclear: only basis is general Labor Code 1720(b) public funds; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts.

reason: Neither the PLHA guidelines nor the County resolution and staff report state a prevailing wage rule, so the trigger stays unclear.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule: the HHAP statute (Health and Safety Code 50220.8, https://california.public.law/codes/health_and_safety_code_section_50220.8) lists eligible uses without any prevailing wage or Labor Code provision, and the County-CoC HHAP MOU and staff report approved by Resolution 26-438 are silent. Locally HHAP funds operations and services, not construction; any capital use would be a general Labor Code 1720(b) question depending on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts.
set.audit_note: Prevailing wage left unclear: no HHAP rule found; only basis would be general Labor Code 1720(b), and current local uses are operating and services.

reason: HHAP statute and the County MOU and staff report contain no prevailing wage rule, so the trigger stays unclear.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: DIR Decision on Administrative Appeal, PW 2006-020 Heber Family Apartments (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-020(A).pdf), following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe Village and PW 2006-005 Central Village: loans of conduit tax-exempt housing revenue bond proceeds, whether publicly offered or privately placed (here a CSCDA issue), are not payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), and federal LIHTCs were treated the same way. The County TEFRA approval adds no public funds. Other public loans in the same deal (for example the trust fund and state HOME loans in Lone Oak II) are evaluated separately and can trigger prevailing wage on their own terms.

reason: DIR PW 2006-020 holds that conduit tax-exempt bond financing is not public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), so the bond financing alone does not trigger prevailing wage.
